subject: Design review: mTLS DNS-resolver shim + SPIFFE-based TLS handoff for private endpoints
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <infra@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Design review: mTLS DNS-resolver shim + SPIFFE-based TLS handoff for private endpoints

Hi Sam / team,

Attaching a short proposal for how Redwood can hand off TLS and DNS responsibilities for private endpoints inside your VPC. This is targeted at customers who want the security of private hostnames + minimal networking changes on their side. Key idea: a tiny DNS-resolver shim (daemonset or VM) runs in-customer-network, performs DoT/mTLS to an upstream resolver, and performs a SPIFFE-based identity exchange with our edge-terminator to enable mutual TLS handoff to private endpoints.

Options (brief):
- Option A — Edge termination + shim-based SPIFFE bootstrap: shim does mTLS to our edge, edge terminates TLS and routes to private backend via internal tunnel. Minimal tenant changes, Redwood manages cert lifecycle.
- Option B — Tenant-sidecar termination: shim obtains certs (SPIFFE X.509) and terminates TLS locally; Redwood routes over tenant-initiated secure channels. More tenant control, extra ops work.
- Option C — Upstream resolver with SRV routing: keep DNS in tenant control, use SRV records to pin traffic to specific terminators. Good for large customers with advanced DNS ops.

Trade-offs (short):
- Latency: A <= C <= B (B can be slightly lower for intra-VPC since termination is local but requires more routing complexity).
- Ops surface: A lowest, B highest.
- Security model: B gives tenant full control of private keys; A uses SPIFFE short-lived identity so no long-lived priv keys in tenant space.

Specific asks / decisions we need from Acme:
1) Which option do you prefer (A/B/C)?
2) Can you open outbound 853 (DoT) and optionally 443 for shim -> resolver/edge?
3) Are you comfortable Redwood managing the SPIFFE trust-anchor inside your VPC (we provide a signed intermediate and an offline bootstrap flow)?
4) Rotation cadence: we propose 7 days (ECDSA P-384) for short-lived certs. Is that acceptable?

Attachments: diagram (high-level flow), csr-template-spiffe.yaml (bootstrap template).

If we can get an answer to the four asks within two business weeks we can lock the lab window and produce a test checklist. Proposed lab window: Apr 20–24.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Jonas,

Thanks for the writeup — this looks promising. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side before we pick option: 

- Network: does the shim require outbound to port 853 only, or will it also need 443/80 for fallback/ACME? Our firewall team is strict and needs the exact list.
- Split-horizon: we run split-horizon for several internal services. How will SRV-based routing (Option C) interact with our resolver topology? Will the shim modify queries or rely on existing resolver behavior?
- Trust model: you mentioned Redwood managing the SPIFFE trust-anchor inside our VPC. We need details on key custody — will we ever see a long-lived private key on our hosts? What auditing can you provide?

Attached: our network policy (acmehealth-network-policy-20260330.pdf) and a short note from platform about acceptable bootstrap flows.

We like SPIFFE in principle, but we need to understand the bootstrap and firewall implications. If you can answer the three bullets we can schedule an internal decision meeting.

—Sam

Sam — quick answers to the bullets and an initial recommendation.

Network: the shim supports two egress modes. By default it will use DoT (TCP/853) to our managed resolvers. We also support HTTPS-based DoH (TCP/443) as a fallback if outbound 853 is blocked. So minimum required outbound ports: 853 (preferred) and 443 (fallback). No inbound ports required.

Split-horizon: the shim acts as a local resolver proxy — it forwards queries unchanged by default, but can be configured with a small policy table to rewrite queries for tenant-private zones (e.g., *.internal.acme). For Option C (SRV routing) the shim can return SRV records that point to internal bridges; it does not need to change upstream resolver behavior. We'll supply a mapping file format.

SPIFFE / key custody: our plan for Option A (recommended for most customers) is:
- Customer runs shim and generates a CSR-like bootstrap token locally (csr-template-spiffe.yaml).
- Redwood validates the bootstrap token via a short, auditable handshake (HMAC-signed request + customer's KMS-provided public key or our one-time JWT).
- Redwood issues a short-lived SPIFFE X.509 (7-day cert, ECDSA P-384) and pushes it to the shim.
- No long-lived private keys leave the customer hosts; the shim generates keys locally and stores them in the platform's configured secret store (customer-managed if they prefer).
For auditing: we can provide issuance logs, signed SVID receipts, and an ACME-like audit bundle for your compliance team.

OCSP / revocation: for short-lived certs (7 days) we prefer OCSP stapling at the edge plus a lightweight internal OCSP responder. CRL is heavy; avoid unless you have a compliance requirement that forces it.

Proposed immediate decisions and owners:
- Decision 1: Adopt Option A (Edge termination + shim SPIFFE bootstrap) — owner: Acme (Sam) — due: 2026-04-12
- Decision 2: Firewall openings 853 + 443 (853 preferred) — owner: Acme network — due: 2026-04-12
- Decision 3: Rotation cadence 7 days / ECDSA P-384 — owner: Redwood (Karthik) — due: 2026-04-12 to confirm implementation
- Decision 4: OCSP stapling + internal responder — owner: Redwood & Acme security — due: 2026-04-12

Action items (short):
- Karthik: produce detailed checklist and a shim config example (by Apr 9).
- Marissa: schedule lab test and provide infra sandbox (by Apr 12).
- Mina: draft rollback & incident playbook (by Apr 16).

I've attached the initial checklist (raceback-checklist-shim-lab.md) and included the CSR template you saw earlier. If that looks good we'll mark Option A as recommended and move to testing.

Thanks,
Karthik

Sam — thanks for the questions and the quick internal review. Summary / decisions so far: 

1) Chosen approach: Option A — Edge termination + shim SPIFFE bootstrap (recommended default).
2) Firewall requirements: outbound TCP 853 (DoT) preferred; allow 443 for DoH fallback. No inbound ports required.
3) Trust model: Redwood will host the short-lived trust-anchor service; customer keys remain local. Bootstrap uses a one-time signed token (customer KMS or offline-signed file) to validate initial CSR. Redwood will provide issuance logs and an audit bundle.
4) Rotation / crypto: 7-day rotation, ECDSA P-384 recommended; OCSP stapling at edge + internal responder for revocation checks.

Next steps & dates:
- Karthik to share detailed checklist and shim config (Apr 9) — DONE (attached).

I've attached the updated diagram and an exported audit-template that you can pass to your compliance team. If Acme is good with Option A and the firewall changes, we'll sign the test window and kick off the lab.
